api_analysis.hypothesis: The illegal memory access in custom_sigmoid is caused by passing host pointers for in_strides/out_strides/shape to the CUDA kernel, because the binding code incorrectly reinterprets int64_t arrays as int* and passes them to the kernel without copying to device memory.
evidence: In custom_ops_binding.cpp, in_strides, out_strides, and shape are declared as int64_t arrays on the host stack.
The launcher signature expects const int* pointers, but the binding passes reinterpret_cast<int*>(in_strides), which points to host memory.
Inside the kernel, these pointers are dereferenced as device pointers (in_strides[d], shape[d]), causing an illegal memory access.
The sanitizer log indicates the crash occurs inside custom_sigmoid_kernel, consistent with accessing invalid memory addresses.
No device-side arrays are allocated or copied for these metadata, so all kernel accesses to them are invalid.
changes: Modify kernels/custom_ops.cu to eliminate the need for device arrays by making the kernel accept stride and shape values as kernel arguments instead of pointers.
Update custom_sigmoid_kernel signature to take in_strides[4], out_strides[4], shape[4] as pass-by-value arrays (or individual parameters).
Adjust custom_sigmoid_launcher to pass the stride and shape values directly.
Similarly update custom_instance_norm2d_kernel and launcher to pass in_strides[4], out_strides[4] as kernel arguments.
Modify kernels/custom_ops_binding.cpp to pass these values as scalar arguments instead of pointers.
Ensure all launches check for CUDA errors after completion.
